skill.name: pangolinfo-amazon-scraper
skill.description: Scrape Amazon product, search, category, seller, and ranking data through Pangolinfo APIs. Return structured JSON, raw HTML, or Markdown for analysis pipelines and agents.
skill.summary: Retrieve structured Amazon product and marketplace data through Pangolinfo parsers.
skill.author: pangolin-spg

security_audit.summary: The static findings mostly match expected scraper behavior, including documented endpoints, HTTP requests, and credential environment variables. The hidden token cache is a real local credential exposure surface, while no prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer an explicit user-configurable credential store, document the local threat model, and keep restrictive permissions with secure deletion and rotation guidance.

remediation.issue: The client reads PANGOLIN_TOKEN, PANGOLIN_EMAIL, and PANGOLIN_PASSWORD from the process environment.
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege credential handling, avoid logging environment values, and recommend token authentication over password-based login.

content.value_statement: Manual Amazon research is slow and difficult to standardize across products, sellers, and search results. This skill retrieves structured marketplace data through Pangolinfo parsers for repeatable analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Scrapes Amazon product detail pages and returns structured product fields.
Runs keyword searches and collects result data through the amzKeyword parser.
Retrieves category listings, seller products, best sellers, and new releases.
Supports JSON, raw HTML, and Markdown response formats.
Uses token authentication or email and password login with automatic token refresh.
limitations: Requires a Pangolinfo account, credentials, available credits, and network access.
Results depend on Pangolinfo availability, Amazon page changes, and regional coverage.
The client does not guarantee completeness, freshness, or accuracy of scraped fields.
The token cache stores credentials locally and requires appropriate host protection.

use_cases.title: Product Research
use_cases.description: Compare prices, ratings, sellers, features, and availability across selected Amazon products.

use_cases.title: Market Monitoring
use_cases.description: Track keyword results, category rankings, best sellers, and new releases for recurring marketplace analysis.

use_cases.title: Data Pipeline Enrichment
use_cases.description: Add normalized Amazon product or seller data to internal reports, research workflows, and agent pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Scrape One Product
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve structured details for this Amazon product URL: [URL]. Use the product detail parser and return the title, brand, price, ratings, seller, availability, and ASIN.

prompt_templates.title: Search a Keyword
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Amazon for [KEYWORD]. Return the first available products with titles, ASINs, prices, ratings, review counts, sponsored status, and delivery information.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Sellers
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect products from this Amazon seller page: [URL]. Group the results by product and summarize price, rating, availability, and delivery fields.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Ranking Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [CATEGORY OR KEYWORD] using Amazon ranking or search results. Return a concise brief covering leading products, price bands, ratings, review volume, seller signals, and notable gaps.

output_examples.input: Product URL for a wireless mouse with the product detail parser.
output_examples.output: A structured product summary containing the ASIN, title, brand, price, rating, review count, availability, seller, features, and product URL.

output_examples.input: Keyword search for noise cancelling headphones.
output: A ranked list of matching products with titles, prices, ratings, review counts, and delivery details.
A result count and source URL for the Amazon search.

output_examples.input: Best sellers request for the home office category.
output_examples.output: A ranking summary with product names, ASINs, rank positions, prices, ratings, and image links when returned by the API.

best_practices: Use token authentication when possible and keep credentials outside prompts, source files, and logs.
Choose the parser that matches the Amazon page type and request only the format your workflow needs.
Respect account credits, regional URLs, service limits, and applicable Amazon terms.
anti_patterns: Do not place Pangolinfo tokens or passwords directly in prompts, scripts, or shared logs.
Do not treat scraped fields as guaranteed current, complete, or authoritative without validation.
Do not issue repeated broad scraping requests without checking credits, scope, and service policies.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: Use PANGOLIN_TOKEN, or provide PANGOLIN_EMAIL and PANGOLIN_PASSWORD for login and token refresh.

faq.question: Which Amazon pages can it scrape?
faq.answer: It supports product details, keyword searches, category listings, seller pages, best sellers, new releases, and related seller variants.

faq.question: Which output formats are available?
faq.answer: The client supports structured JSON, raw HTML, and Markdown responses.

faq.question: Can it search by keyword?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a keyword with the query option, and the client builds an Amazon search URL for the keyword parser.

faq.question: Does it cache authentication tokens?
faq.answer: Yes. The client can store a token at ~/.pangolin_token, so protect the host and review local credential policies.

faq.question: What affects scraping results?
faq.answer: Results depend on the selected parser, Amazon region, page state, Pangolinfo service availability, credits, and response fields.
